characters.name: Diane Lockhart
characters.description: See her folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Author Tract: Her rants about Trump. Broken Ace: ThroughCreator Breakdownabout Trump.The Good Wifeshowed her to be a brilliant attorney, but she now never does court cases, preferring to join the Resistance. Divorce Is Temporary: She and Kurt are separated throughout Season 1 and 2 for often good reasons (their different politics and his affair), but they get back together in Season 3 and appear happy. Good Adultery, Bad Adultery: The "good adultery" to Kurt's "bad". She cheated on him with a fellow disillusioned liberal, but is given a more sympathetic treatment due to Kurt cheating first.

characters.name: Maia Rindell
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: While she's definitely attracted to women, it's also hinted that she's at leastsomewhatinterested in men, as she had a boyfriend prior to getting into a relationship with Amy, and there's hints of romantic tension between her and Blum in her final couple of episodes. The Apprentice: Is a protege of Diane, her godmother and an associate. Became Their Own Antithesis: At the start of the series she's pretty anti-Donald Trump(if not quite as vocally so as Diana), and is trying to make up for her family's misdeeds by becoming an honest lawyer. By the time she leaves, she's transformed into anAmoral Attorneyunder the tutelage of Roland Blum, and they leave for Washington D.C. to set up a law firm, implicitly intending to work with the Trump administration. But Not Too Gay: Weirdly, this became the case more and more for her as the show went on. During Season 1 she was frequently shown with her girlfriend Amy. In Season 2 Amy only got a couple of appearances before falling victim toChuck Cunningham Syndromeat the end of the season, despite it being mentioned in Amy's last appearance that the two were considering getting engaged. By the time of Season 3, Maia's sexual preferences aren't mentioned even once throughout the whole season, and her last few episodes even seem to imply some sexual tension between her andBlum. Expy: She starts out as this show's version of Alicia Florrick, namely someone whose life is derailed by criminal scandals involving herBig, Screwed-Up Family, and has to rely on a favor from an old friend in order to get their legal career back on-track. During Season 3, however, she becomes something more akin toKim Wexler, in that her career plans go south after she's mistreated by her bosses, and she chooses to work with a larger than lifeAmoral Attorney, embraces their approach to the law, and attempts to make life difficult for her former employers in revenge for both their treatment of her and causing her partner to (at least temporaril

characters.name: Lucca Quinn
characters.description: See her folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Belligerent Sexual Tension: With Colin, although it calms down a lot once he'sPut on a Bus. Icon of Rebellion: Played with. As Luca is black and Colin is white, making her son mixed-race to two political figures, Lucca is often pushed into taking some kind of political stance, which she does (such as her#MotheringWhileBlackcampaign), but also tries to resist the overt political manipulations of the role. Mama Bear: Becomes this to her and Colin's son. Power Hair: She has short hair and becomes a powerful divorce lawyer.

characters.name: Adrian Boseman
characters.description: Amicable Exes: With Liz. Bald of Authority: He is bald and in charge of his law firm. Benevolent Boss: He is very caring of the people who work for him. Broken Pedestal: After discovering how Carl Riddick abused countless women over the years, Adrian has a hard time understanding how a man he respected as a fearless fighter for social justice could treat the women under him as nothing but sexual toys. Hidden Depths: Is shown in one episode to have started taking a French cooking class and apparently being quite good at it.

characters.name: Marissa Gold
characters.description: See her folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Ambiguously Bi: Downplayed; it's hinted that she's at least bi-curious, given some of her remarks about Maia and Carmen (as well as kissing the former during their last on-screen interaction and only rejecting any idea of going any further on the grounds that they'reBetter as Friends), but she's only ever seen dating and being intimate with men, and ultimately marries one near the end of the series. Ambiguously Jewish: Not so ambiguous in the original, but she mentions that she went to Jerusalem but generally doesn't comment on the Jewish issues the firm often confronts, such as Neo-Nazis. Badass Israeli: Downplayed as she isn't a soldier — at least not currently, though it's indicated that she briefly served in the Israeli Defense Force when she was younger, even if she didn't see frontline service — but she's a former charity worker in Israel who responds very calmly to crisis, such as Maya being targeted by Kill All Lawyers. Daddy's Little Villain: Deconstructed. Marissa is very moral, but has inherited her father's more dubious morals. She's more likely to take the attitude that people are more important than politics (see: choosing to help Julius), which apparently horrifies the Democratic Eli.

characters.name: Barbara Kolstad
characters.description: Satellite Character: She's the boss throughout Seasons 1, and in the pilot episode is presented as hesitant to allow Diane to join the firm, but we learn almost nothing about her before she leaves in Season 2. Put on a Bus: Very abruptly leaves Reddick, Boseman & Kolstad in the Season 2 premiere to join Renee's firm, and is not seen again afterward. The show does not even reveal anyone's reaction to her leaving the firm aside from Diane's — at least until Season 5, when it's revealed that many of the other senior partners, Liz included, blame Diane for forcing her out.

characters.name: Colin Morrello
characters.description: Dating Catwoman: Dates Lucca even though they're from rival firms. Nice Guy: Unlike most at his firm, he is a genuinely sweet person. Hero Antagonist: Not a bad guy, just a prosecutor doing his job, however his cases sometimes have him against the Boseman firm. Put on a Bus: To Washington between Seasons 2 and 3.

characters.name: JayDiPersia
characters.description: Afro Ass Kicker: Sometimes, such as when he and Lucca are attacked by Nazis in Season 3. The Big Guy: Jay is very tall and usually plays the role of a necessary badass. Bruiser with a Soft Center: His badass behavior is often just necessary in support of the firm, and in reality, Jay is pretty gentle. Genius Bruiser: Jay is a very tough investigator who is also highly intelligent and loves art. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: The "huge guy" to Marissa's "tiny girl".

characters.name: Julius Cain
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: He's often mocked and derided by his co-workers for his conservative political views, even though it's strongly implied that he doesn't support Donald Trump specifically and only voted for him because he happened to be the Republican candidate in 2016 and 2020. Commuting on a Bus: During Season 4, when he becomes a judge, but still makes reasonably regular appearances on the show. He's stripped of his position and jailed on false corruption charges for his attempts to investigate Memo 618, but gets caught up in a mass-pardon of judges by Trump near the end of his first term, and returns to working for Reddick & Lockhart early in Season 5. Put on a Bus: A temporary, blink-and-you'll-miss-it example; he goes off to work for a Trump-supportive firm near the end of the first season, only to come back at the start of the second season with just a brief comment that the firm he worked for was ineptly-run and on the verge of going out of business.

characters.name: Liz Reddick
characters.description: Amicable Exes: With Adrian. Daddy's Girl: Deconstructed. Both she and Carl were committed to racial justice and she followed him into profession, but she's realistic about Carl's neglectful treatment of she and her mother even before she learns that he was a serial rapist. Legacy Character: To Carl, her father. Sins of the Father:In multiple episodes, Liz has to pay for the fact that her father, Carl, was a rapist (without her knowledge), but this is justified because she chose to make the victims signNDAs.Less justified is Ri'Chard deciding to try and take the firm down while Liz is at the helm. While Ri'Chard turns out to havedamngood reason for being bitter towards Carl, who cruelly humiliated him back when he was first starting out and struggling financially, Liz had nothing to do with that and no way of knowing what her father did. When she finds out, she agrees it was messed up. Ri'Chard does later drop his grudge after becoming genuinely fond of Liz, though. In multiple episodes, Liz has to pay for the fact that her father, Carl, was a rapist (without her knowledge), but this is justified because she chose to make the victims signNDAs.

characters.name: Roland Blum
characters.description: Amoral Attorney:Oh God, yes.Immoralis an even better descriptor. Ambiguously Bi: Is only seen embracing or kissing women, flirting with Maia, saying he slept with Marissa's mother. But, it is suggested that he has had sex with his nude, Chinese man-servant and Marissa suggests that Roy Cohn had sex with him he agrees it happened. Captain Ersatz: While his personal mannerisms are based on those of Roy Cohn, he also bears some very strong similarities toSaulGoodman, in that both are larger-than-lifeAmoral Attorneyswith Irish ancestry who work in obviously unprofessional surroundings and get up to all sorts of absurdCourtroom Anticsand blatantly illegal acts with minimal consequences. At least until they both lose their ability to practise the law and have to resort to other means to continue their careers until they can resume doing so (in Blum's case by moving to Washington D.C.; in Goodman's case until he serves a suspension of his law license). Fat Slob: He often strips off although he's not fat per se, but is shown to be extremely messy, rude, and undignified. The Friend Nobody Likes: No one likes having to work with him, and will go to lengths to get out of it if they can.

characters.name: David Lee
characters.description: See his folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Actually Pretty Funny: When a former employee writers a play with thinly veiled caricatures of the main lawyers, everyone else finds it horrifying while David can't stop laughing throughout the show. The Bus Came Back: He gets indirectlyPut on a Busfollowing the series premiere, as he remains at Diane's old firm while the setting moves to Reddick, Boseman & Kolstad. In Season 4 he comes back working for STR Laurie. Out of Focus: He's missing for most of Season 6 and only comes back for one episode so that he can be written out of the show for good. Lee himself lampshades this, saying he hasn't been down to the Reddick & Ri'Chard floor for a while.

characters.name: Gavin Firth
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: After finally making his motives clear at the end of season 4 when RBL tries to buy back their firm. He disappears without a trace in season 5 with David Lee taking over as STR's mouthpiece in the firm.

characters.name: Carmen Moyo
characters.description: Amoral Attorney: Played with, due to making a good connection with a client on her first day she quickly becomes the go-to lawyer for the criminal underworld in Chicago. She knows they're all guilty but she still does what every lawyer in the show does to defend her clients. Even opposing lawyers using guilt tripping tactics on her ultimately fall flat because of her stoicism. Butch Lesbian: She's revealed to be this halfway through Season 6 — and dating a woman who looks like Marissa, at that, leading to a very awkward situation when this comes out into the open. Sixth Ranger Traitor: After a season and a half of being on the show, it's revealed that she was given her job by STR Laurie so that she could spy on how things were turning out at the company in the wake of Adrian's departure, and considers her loyalty to be to them first and foremost. Ultimately, nothing much comes of this, as Ri'Chard ends up taking over the running of STR Laurie, leaving Carmen loyal to them either way. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: A downplayed example; like Lucca, who'sPut on a Busin the episode before Carmen arrives, she's an African-American lawyer withBoyish Short Hair, who's not afraid to speak up for herself and becomes fast friends with Marissa. However, she shows her share ofDivergent Character Evolutionby being much more willing than Lucca to take on morally-questionable clients, and also being far less loyal to the company, even if it never causes any serious issues.

characters.name: Hal Wackner
characters.description: Kangaroo Court: He is trying to avert this with his court by doing things like having the defendants, plaintiffs, and witnesses wear mascot quits to keep the jury from being biased due to race or appearance. But as Marissa points out in the finale, his court only has power as long as the rulings he make are accepted by the plaintiffs and defendants.The moment a plaintiff admits he will just go make his own community court to get the verdict he wants completely undermines Wackner's Court and leads into the final montage showing community courts popping up everywhere and giving out random and contradicting verdicts that ultimately don't matter. Rage Breaking Point: Marissa pushes him to the point by questioning his integrity in front of his court. Moments after kicking her out he immediately regrets it because he realizes she was correct and he was biased. Too Proud for Lowly Work: Averted, the final episode of season 5 reveals that he is theJanitorat the copy shop his court was being hosted. And he has no problem continue to do the work even after the court is trashed in the riot.

characters.name: Dr. Lyle Bettencourt
characters.description: Dr. Feelgood:Inverted, he administers Ketamine therapy, but it's in a controlled environment and under his supervision. And a session always ends with a debriefprovided a bomb doesn't go off outside. Romantic Runner-Up: Despite a clear romantic attraction between him and Diane throughout Season 6, in the end Diane chooses to stay loyal to Kurt. Lyle takes it reasonably well, knowing that Kurt's a good man.

characters.name: Ri'Chard Lane
characters.description: Bait-and-Switch Tyrant: His first appearance gives the impression that he's going to come into the firm and completely disrupt the team's dynamic. While his arrival does shake things up a bit, he actually does prove to be aReasonable Authority Figure. And then the trope getsDouble Subvertedwhen he reveals that hedidintend to destroy the firm (or at least leave it unrecognizable) in revenge for Carl Reddick humiliating him in a job interview years earlier, but realized how wrong it would have been to do so. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He could give Elsbeth a run for her money with quirks, but he is still an incredibly competent lawyer just like the rest of the cast, even screwing over STR Laurie. Good Parents: Liz starts to warm to him after she has dinner at his house and finds out that he's an attentive and loving father. My Nayme Is: He admits to Liz and her son that his real name is just plain old Richard Lane, but he changed the spelling to Ri'Chard to stand out more. Platonic Co-Parenting: Liz is surprised when she goes to his house and finds he lives with multiple women, unsure which one is Mrs. Lane. He explains that Mrs. Lane sadly passed away some time ago, so her best friend and sister help him with the child-rearing, and he helps them with their children. They all live together because it's easier.

characters.name: Tom & Jerry
characters.description: Those Two Guys: You never see one without the other. Shout-Out: Their names are Thomas and Jeremy, but everyone calls themTom and Jerry.

characters.name: Mike Kresteva
characters.description: Revenge by Proxy: It's strongly implied that he's going after Diane and Maia as a very convoluted form of proxy revenge for Peter Florrick's beating him in the Illinois gubernatorial election several years earlier, even though Peter had long-since left the office in disgrace (right after the embarrassing failure of his presidential primary bid, to boot), and Diane barely even had anything to do with Peter's campaign.

characters.name: Henry Rindell
characters.description: Eviler than Thou: To Lenore, somewhat. Maia thinks that Lenore is the worst parent, as she cheated on him with his brother, but Lenore can't put Maia in prison and Henry can. Faux Affably Evil: Everything about Henry's early appearances would suggest that he's kind and extremely protective of Maia, despite being a fraudster. Then he tries to frameherand is willing to make her the scapegoat, and it swiftly becomes apparent what a self-serving villain he is. Give Him a Normal Life: Deconstructed. Heapparentlywanted this for Maia...but in fact manipulated her for years to be unknowingly party to his fraud, by running shell corporations and charities for him. Manipulative Bastard: There's nothing he wouldn't do to get the upper hand on Maia (and, ideally, put her in prison for his crimes). Put on a Bus to Hell: After going to prison.

characters.name: Lenore Rindell
characters.description: Even Evil Has Standards: She knew about and was complicit in her husband's fraud and attempts to implicate Maia, and she has an affair with his brother, but when it comes to it, she cracks and admits that Maia knew nothing, allowing her to go free. Though it may be a downplayed example, as it's implied that she was originally willing to go through with selling out Maia until Diane talked her out of it. Settle for Sibling: She's married to Henry but cheats on him with his brother Jax. Put on a Bus to Hell: She gets sent to prison in-between Season 1 and 2, and re-appears a few episodes into Season 2 when the state unsuccessfully tries to get her to testify against her daughter. Maia tells her father that the feds have offered to release her with time served if they hand him over, but seeing how Lenore is never seen or mentioned again afterwards it's not clear how truthful she was being.

characters.name: KurtMcVeigh
characters.description: See his folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Divorce Is Temporary: He and Diane separate throughout Season 1 and 2, but Season 3 shows them to be back together and (mostly) happy. Everyone Has Standards: Despite his right-wing political views, he didn't vote for Trump in the 2016 election; instead, he wrote in Ted Cruz. Good Adultery, Bad Adultery: The "bad" to Diane's "good". When he cheated on her with Holly, he broke Diane's trust and so it's treated as much more moral when she cheats on him although they're still together. Pet the Dog: When he tells Diane he didn't vote for Trump.

characters.name: Amy Breslin
characters.description: Closet Key: For Maia as far as we know. Lipstick Lesbian: Is a lesbian and as feminine as Maia. Satellite Love Interest: She's FBI but we don't learn anything about her or her past. What Happened to the Mouse?: Amy is completely absent in Season 3, despite there being no explicit reference to her and Maia breaking up prior to this. The two were shown to still be together even after Amy testified against Maia for the FBI, and there was even talk of them getting engaged. It's possible that Maia broke up with her shortly after having sex with Carrine at the office, but it's never given a follow-up. Notably, Amy isn't brought up at any point during Maia's firing from Reddick, Boseman & Lockhart or subsequent exit from Chicago and one scene shows Maia and Marissa tempted to engage in a romantic moment, implying that she's no longer in the picture.

characters.name: Felix Staples
characters.description: A flame-baiting, controversial alt-right internet personality. Attention Whore: So much so that when his ban on the show's equivalent toRedditis lifted, he gets angered because it means he can no longer argue with Reddick, Boseman and Kolstad's panel. Blatant Lies: When put on the witness stand in Season 3, he denies being part of the alt-right, claiming that he's actually more of a libertarian and would have voted for Gary Johnson in 2016, but voted for Donald Trump because he could tell Johnson had no chance of victory, and considered Trump the more palatable choice between him and Hillary Clinton — all of which totally flies against everything he's said in he previous appearances. Camp Gay: Downplayed; he is openly gay and dresses in pretty flashy clothes, but doesn't really have any particularly campy mannerisms. Expy: Of Milo Yiannopoulos, a flamboyant gay personality and online conservative who worked for Breitbart News.

characters.name: Carl Reddick
characters.description: The founding partner of Reddick, Boseman & Kolstad, and a renowned civil rights lawyer, largely retired when the series begins. Broken Pedestal: Despite being a civil rights icon during his lifetime, after his death it turns out that he had a track record of sexually harassing his employees, forcing the surviving partners to cover up his misdeeds. Expy: For Jonas Stern fromThe Good Wife, as they're both veteran lawyers who have largely become silent partners in their firms at the time the series begins, but come back to cause issues during the first season. Unlike Stern, however, who cashed out his shares in Stern, Lockhart & Gardner and took his clients with him, plunging the firm into financial disarray, Reddick simply reverts back to being a silent partner after his attempt to depose Adrian fails, and then dies — with Liz inheriting his shares and taking his named partner's role at the company — before he has the chance to cause any further problems. Or at least,directlycause any further problems... Posthumous Character: Played with; we actually do see him when he's alive, but it's after his death that he has the biggest impact on the plot, when the truth of his sexual harassment incidents comes out into the open, something that hangs over the firm and Liz for the rest of the show's run. We Hardly Knew Ye: He appears in one episode in the first season, then is revealed to have died off-screen by the start of the second season. In a subversion, the partners find out more than they ever wanted to know about him during the third season.

characters.name: Louis Canning
characters.description: See his folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Demoted to Extra: Unlike inThe Good Wife, where he was one of the show's most prominent recurring characters, Canning only appears in two episodes of this series and barely even does anything of any importance to the plot; his role could have been filled by any other lawyer without making much of a difference.

characters.name: The First Lady
characters.description: Melania Trump herself. Or at least, a very good impersonator. Awful Wedded Life: She claims to be suffering from this, allegedly wanting to divorceDonald Trumpand asking for Diane's help on the matter. Riddle for the Ages: It's never exactly made clear whether the character we see in the show is the real Melania, or just someone pretending to be her for the purposes of either pranking Diana or causing some kind of scandal for the Democratic Party.

characters.name: Gary Carr
characters.description: A British actor, famous forDownton Abbey, who is hired by Roland Blum to pretend to be his paralegal. Adam Westing: Downplayed; Carr acts mostly the same as his real-life counterpart, until his final scene where he's revealed to be a Scientologist and tries to recruit Lucca. Church of Happyology: In his final scene he reveals that he's a Scientologist, and tries to recruit Lucca to his religion. Whether or not Lucca has anything against Scientologists in general isn't clear, but she's definitely annoyed enough by the idea that Gary was only ever getting close to her as a way of converting her to his religion to rebuff any further attempts at contact by him. Classically Trained Extra: It's revealed that he accepted Blum's request to pretend to be his paralegal as a way of training for a lawyer role he's been hired for, even though it only includes a couple of scenes.

characters.name: Howard Lyman
characters.description: A former partner from Diane's old law firm, who later becomes a federal judge. See his folder atThe Good Wife'scharacter page. Tropes exclusive toThe Good Fightgo here. Kicked Upstairs: From what he says during his first appearance as a judge, it seems like he was encouraged by his former partners — apparently mostly by David Lee, though he isn't mentioned by name — to take up the role as a way of getting him out of his former company. What Happened to the Mouse?:Howard appears in the pilot episode, then again in the second season premiere to set up his role as a judge, and is never seen again, likely because of Jerry Adler's retirement from acting in 2019.Jackie is never seen or mentioned in this series, leaving it unclear whether their relationship ever went anywhere. Howard appears in the pilot episode, then again in the second season premiere to set up his role as a judge, and is never seen again, likely because of Jerry Adler's retirement from acting in 2019.
